paragraphs.text: CDLS4 is a cohesinopathy caused by heterozygous variants in RAD21. Affected individuals have growth retardation, minor skeletal anomalies, and facial features that overlap Cornelia de Lange syndrome (CdLS). Compared with CdLS caused by NIPBL, SMC1A, or SMC3 mutations, the phenotype is attenuated, and cognitive impairment is usually much milder (Deardorff et al., 2012; Krab et al., 2020). Some individuals with monoallelic RAD21 variants have holoprosencephaly, with or without CdLS characteristics (Krab et al., 2020).

(2020) later listed this boy (family F21) as patient 2 of Deardorff et al. (2012) and as the patient of McBrien et al. (2008). paragraphs.text: Krab et al. (2020) reported 49 individuals from 33 families with RAD21 alterations, 24 of whom were previously unpublished. The 29 patients with full clinical information (cohort A) had an attenuated CdLS phenotype compared with patients with NIPBL or SMC1A variants, particularly for facial morphology, limb anomalies, cognition, and behavior. In cohort A, they found postnatal microcephaly in 16 of 28, postnatal short stature in 10 of 27, synophrys in 19 of 28, a long and/or smooth philtrum in 26 of 29, a short fifth finger in 23 of 28, cleft palate in 6 of 25, heart anomalies in 9 of 23, hearing loss in 8 of 24, and gastroesophageal reflux in 13 of 25. None of the 29 had major limb malformations. Short stature and microcephaly typically developed postnatally. Unusual anomalies included vertebral anomalies (clefts and hemivertebrae) and relatively frequent malformations of foregut-derived structures. Sixteen of 29 patients (55%) had normal or mildly impaired cognition, and all patients aged 3 years or older used some words. Fourteen of 25 had behavioral problems, mainly anxiety, ADHD, autism spectrum disorder, and obsessive-compulsive behavior; aggression and self-injurious behavior each occurred in only 1 patient.
